---
title: "Get started with surveyframe"
description: "Install R, RStudio and surveyframe, open an example study in SurveyStudio, then turn a downloaded template into your own study, by point and click in SurveyStudio."
---

SurveyStudio is surveyframe's visual workspace. It opens from RStudio, so the
setup has 3 parts: R, RStudio and the surveyframe package. All 3 are free.
Setup takes about 15 minutes the first time.

## What you need

- A computer running Windows, macOS or Linux, with permission to install
  software.
- An internet connection for the installation.

## 1. Install R

Download R for your system from [CRAN](https://cran.r-project.org/) and run
the installer with its default settings.

## 2. Install RStudio

Download RStudio Desktop from
[Posit](https://posit.co/download/rstudio-desktop/) and run the installer.
Then open RStudio. Its window has a pane named **Console**, usually at the
bottom left, with a `>` prompt.

## 3. Install surveyframe

Click in the Console beside the `>` prompt, paste this line and press Enter:

```r
install.packages("surveyframe")
```

R downloads surveyframe and the packages it uses. This takes a few minutes.
The installation has finished when the `>` prompt returns. The
**Addins** menu in RStudio's toolbar now lists the surveyframe commands.

## 4. Open an example study

In RStudio, open the **Addins** menu, choose **surveyframe: Try a demo** and
pick a study. It opens in SurveyStudio on the Design screen, with its
questionnaire, analysis plan and demonstration responses loaded, so every
stage has something to show.

![SurveyStudio's Design screen with the training evaluation example open: the questionnaire's questions are listed in the centre and the screens in the left menu.](../templates/paired/design.png){width=100%}

## 5. Start your own study from a template

Each [questionnaire template](templates.html) has a **download the
instrument (.sframe)** link. To make it your own study:

1. Download the `.sframe` file from the template page and save it in your
   project folder.
2. In RStudio, open the **Addins** menu and choose
   **surveyframe: Open analysis workspace**.
3. In SurveyStudio's left menu, choose **Open Instrument**, then
   **Browse .sframe file**, and select the file.
4. On the Design screen, edit the title, the questions and the answer
   options for your study. Choose **Plan** to adapt the research questions,
   then press **Save to Studio**.
5. On the Report screen, press **Download copy** to save your study as a new
   `.sframe` file. If SurveyStudio offers **Save as a new instrument**, tick
   it, since your study starts a new record. This is the file to keep, share
   with your supervisor and use to collect responses.

The downloaded template has no responses. Your own responses arrive once you
collect them, as
[Run a study in SurveyStudio](run-a-study-in-surveystudio.html) shows.
